one_liner: Safe-Rust WHATWG URL parser with a zero-copy fast path for canonical URLs; 3.4-4.1x faster than the url crate on ASCII.
what_it_does: A WHATWG URL Standard parser meant to replace servo's url crate. It passes all 891 WPT urltestdata cases and all 278 setter cases in its test tree. The API reuses rust-url's names (parse, join, make_relative, path_segments_mut, query_pairs_mut, set_port(Option<u16>), from/to_file_path) and adds WHATWG setters and a SearchParams type, but the type is Url<'a> because it borrows its input whenever it can. Optional features add serde and an http::Uri bridge, the crate supports no_std + alloc, and a separate C ABI (sorug-ffi) ships only as GitHub Release binaries.
how_it_is_fast: A pre-pass (src/parser/fast.rs) handles absolute special URLs that have no base URL and are already canonical. It recognizes the scheme with one masked 64-bit little-endian compare (https://, http://, file:///, ftp://, ws(s)://). It finds delimiters with SWAR zero-byte detection (haszero(word ^ splat(c))) for spans under 64 bytes and memchr for longer ones, and checks each byte against 256-entry lookup tables. If nothing needs rewriting, the Url borrows the input string (Backing::Borrowed) and makes no heap allocation. The record is the href string plus eight u32 component offsets and a flag byte, like rust-url's layout. Any input that needs normalization falls through to a full WHATWG state machine that writes into an owned buffer. IDN labels made only of Latin-1 lowercase, CJK, kana or Hangul characters skip NFC and the Bidi/joiner checks and go straight to Punycode.
when_to_use: High-volume parsing of already-normalized absolute http(s)/ws(s)/ftp/file URLs (crawl frontiers, access logs, config) where the source &str outlives the Url. This is the zero-allocation path, and the project's CI measured it at about 3.5-4.4x faster than url 2.5.
You need pure safe Rust. The main crate has forbid(unsafe_code) and needs no C++ toolchain, unlike the ada-url bindings.
no_std + alloc or wasm32-unknown-unknown targets that need WHATWG semantics. CI checks both.
You want Node/Ada/WPT-aligned results where rust-url differs, such as keeping empty file: path segments, rejecting an empty '@' authority, and stricter IDNA Bidi/joiner checks.
Mixed real-world URL streams, as long as you plan for roughly a 1.6x gain over url (the 8-URL batch in the project's CI) rather than the 3-4x single-URL headline.
when_not_to_use: Long or unusual IDN hosts. The IDNA_Long_ACE case, which the README table omits, took about 11 us in three CI runs, against 3.6-4.0 us for url and about 4.9 us for ada-url (2.8-3.2x slower than url). On the ordinary IDN case, the gain over url is only about 1.2x.

Inputs that are not canonical: uppercase scheme or host, explicit default ports, dot segments, backslashes, characters that need percent-encoding, IPv4-like hosts, or anything parsed against a base. These take the full parser and allocate, and the published numbers do not measure them.

Production code that needs a stable, proven dependency. It is on 0.x (minor bumps may break), has a single author, 1 star, 442 total downloads and 0 reverse dependencies, and went from 0.1.0 to 0.6.2 in nine days (2026-08-01 to 2026-08-09). 1.0 is held until the fuzz reliability clocks pass.

Code that must match rust-url output exactly, or that hands url::Url to other crates. The divergences are intentional and documented, and there is no url::Url conversion, so a crate that needs url::Url still has to re-parse the string.
You need URLPattern, an RFC 3986 mode, or detailed parse errors. The project lists these as non-goals, and ParseError stays Failure | InputTooLong through 1.0.

integration.dependencies: memchr 2.7 and unicode-normalization 0.1 (both no-default-features); optional serde 1 and http 1. build.rs generates IDNA range tables from the vendored Unicode 17.0.0 UCD files (about 1.2 MB of text shipped in the crate). A C cdylib/staticlib plus sorug.h is available from GitHub Releases only.
integration.platforms: Any Rust target. SWAR is portable u64 code with no arch-specific intrinsics, and memchr picks SIMD itself. CI checks no_std on wasm32. File-path and socket helpers need std on unix, windows, redox, wasi or hermit. Prebuilt FFI binaries exist for linux-x86_64, macos-aarch64 and windows-x86_64.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Url<'a> is plain data (a &str or String plus u32 offsets, no interior mutability), so it is Send + Sync through Rust auto traits. Origin::new_opaque uses a global AtomicUsize counter.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the method names follow rust-url (the cookbook has a migration table), but Url carries a lifetime (call into_owned() to get 'static), host() returns the host string instead of rust-url's typed Host (use host_parsed()), ParseError has only two variants, and results follow WHATWG/Node where rust-url differs

gotchas: The zero-copy result borrows the input. Storing it, returning it, or using FromStr/TryFrom<&str> (which call into_owned) allocates a copy, which gives back part of the benchmarked advantage.
The fast path runs only for Url::parse with no base URL. join() and parse_with_base always go through the full state machine and allocate.

UTS #46 value mapping is hand-written: NFKC plus to_lowercase plus a list of special cases. The Unicode 17 tables supply only membership (disallowed, Bidi, joiners), and the module doc calls the mapping 'deliberately small ... enough for the WPT urltestdata suite'. WPT and differential fuzzing against Node, Ada and rust-url are the safety net, so rare-script hosts could still diverge from ICU.
rust-url's host() returns a typed Host, but sorug's host() returns Option<&str>. Code ported by name hits type errors, and code that wants the typed value must call host_parsed().
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick sorug over Ada (C++) or its ada-url Rust bindings when you want pure safe Rust with no C++ build, a rust-url-shaped API, and mostly canonical ASCII input that can stay borrowed. ada-rs and lucid-url are measured against native C++ Ada, while sorug's Ada numbers go through the ada-url FFI crate, so the numbers across these entries are not directly comparable; for IDN-heavy input or production-critical parsing, Ada's maturity is the safer choice.
verified_claims_summary: The README Criterion table (measured 2026-08-07 on 'Linux' with lto and codegen-units=1; no CPU model or rustc version given) shows sorug at 28.3, 56.0, 196 and 31.1 ns against url 2.5 at 97, 216, 248 and 129 ns on four single URLs, three of which are already canonical and hit the zero-allocation path; ada-url (Rust bindings to C++ Ada) falls between the two except on IDNA, where it is slowest. The project's own informational CI job (GitHub ubuntu-24.04 runner, rustc 1.98.1, 20 samples, 2026-09-20) shows the same ordering at about twice the absolute times: 3.5x, 4.4x, 1.16x and 4.1x faster than url, 1.66x on an 8-URL mixed batch, and 3.2x slower than url on a long-ACE IDN host.
status_note: Maintained but young. The last release is 0.6.2 (2026-08-09), the only commits since are bot refreshes of the WPT fixtures, the author has frozen features and performance work until a 1.0 that waits on 30 days of daily and 8 weeks of weekly fuzz runs passing, and daily fuzz and CI runs pass; dual MIT/Apache-2.0 on crates.io.
